newsitem.title: RUSSIA: OLYMPICS-ST PETERSBURG RELIEVED BY OLYMPIC REPORT.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-ST PETERSBURG RELIEVED BY OLYMPIC REPORT.

text.p: St Petersburg's supporters are convinced their chances of hosting the 2004 Olympics have improved following the city's evaluation report from the International Olympics Committee (IOC).

"With this evaluation, which is very positive, I will be able to sleep peacefully now," said Alexander Kozlovsky, vice-president of the Russian Olympic Committee, in charge of promoting the St Petersburg Games.
"I knew it would be difficult for us to take part in the contest, but now I am convinced we have a very good chance."

Russia's money troubles -- and the fact Soviet Moscow hosted the Games just 17 years ago in 1980 -- have nevertheless left St. Petersburg an outsider in the race to hold the 2004 Olympics against wealthier contenders as Rome, Stockholm and Cape Town.
But the Russian government argue that hosting the event in the city formerly known as Leningrad would put an international stamp of approval on its efforts to replace communism with democracy.

Kozlovsky said the Russians had managed to convince the commission of the main point -- that the Olympics would not strain the state budget since the bulk of the money is already committed for the city's tercentenary.
